meta.purpose: TWO illustrations per plant: a flat iconic CATALOGUE (seed-packet) image, and a naturalistic IN-POT (growth-habit) image. Same plant, two styles, swapped by context.

catalogue.look: flat, painterly, iconic — bold simplified gouache + coloured-pencil with a soft paper texture; a SINGLE hero bloom (or one characterful leaf/sprig for foliage plants), saturated yet gentle; decorative, in the spirit of a modern seed-packet / field-guide icon
catalogue.framing: one specimen element centred, generous margin, on a FULLY TRANSPARENT background — no circle, no pot, no soil, no text, no label, no shadow

container.use: the plant as it appears planted in the pot
container.look: naturalistic botanical field-guide illustration of the WHOLE plant in its growth habit, soft realistic shading and fine veining (matches the existing salvia / coleus / calibrachoa art)
container.framing: whole plant, head-on side view, role-shaped (thriller upright / filler mound / spiller trailing), vertically centred, on a FULLY TRANSPARENT background — no pot, no soil, no ground, no text, no shadow
container.output: PNG with alpha, ~1024×1536 portrait (spillers may be taller)

roleForms.thrill: upright "thriller" — tall and vertical, height-giving, distinctly taller than wide
roleForms.fill: mounding "filler" — a rounded, bushy mound, fuller and wider than tall
roleForms.spill: trailing "spiller" — a cascading spray that hangs downward, fullest at the crown and tapering into long trailing stems, as if draping over a pot rim

pipeline: For each plant generate BOTH images (catalogue + container) on transparent backgrounds.
Trim each to its content bounds (~10px pad).
Save container art to plants/<id>.png and catalogue art to catalog/<id>.png.

Register: GardenArt.setContainerImage(id,{href,w,h}) and GardenArt.setCatalogImage(id,{href,w,h}); w/h are design units preserving the trimmed aspect (container thriller h≈200, filler h≈150, spiller h≈175).
meta.reference: salvia, coleus and calibrachoa already exist in the CONTAINER style — match them for the in-pot art.
